requirements.text: Create a critical case via Alert Channel
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 3 AND contact_id = 1 AND product_id = 48 AND priority = 'critical' AND channel = 'alert'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (1233 after 1232); the task creates one case
Acme Systems is account 3; MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 28 is product 48, not the products named Variant 8, 48, 68 or 88
contact 1 (Michael Ward, primary) is the only contact of Acme Systems, and the policy requires the reporting contact of the account
priority critical and channel alert as stated

requirements.text: assign it to CSM Tier 1 Support
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assignment_group_id = 1
assumptions: CSM Tier 1 Support is group 1, not its suffixed namesakes (groups 21, 41 and 61)

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 1 AND user_id = 6
assumptions: Stephanie Todd is user 6, an active agent, a member of groups 35 and 50 but not of group 1 in the seed
the group is the one the case is assigned to, CSM Tier 1 Support; the policy also requires assigned_to to be a member of assignment_group_id
id assumed next in sequence (960 after 959); the task creates one membership

requirements.text: assign the case directly to Stephanie Todd
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assigned_to = 6
assumptions: Stephanie Todd is user 6

requirements.text: Make sure that asset is moved to the repair status so no new workloads are directed there
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 14 AND status = 'repair'
assumptions: the asset is the server running MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 28 at Acme Systems: installed product 14 (serial P48-657716-2595), the account's only installed product of product 48, in_use in the seed

requirements.text: Make sure that asset is moved to the repair status so no new workloads are directed there
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE account_id = 3 AND installed_product_id <> 14 AND status = 'repair'
assumptions: boundary of 'that asset': Acme Systems' other installed products, including the HPE ProLiant and Dell PowerEdge servers a loose reading of 'the server' could take, stay out of repair

requirements.text: Once the case is ready for work, apply the toughest resolution SLA for critical priority
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1233 AND sla_def_id = 6 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: the toughest resolution SLA for critical priority is SLA Resolution - Critical (sla_def 6, 240 minutes), the only active resolution definition for critical
stage in_progress kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and SLAs pause only while a case is pending
selected by case and definition, not by id: every seed case carries a response and a resolution SLA, so the new row's id depends on whether a response SLA is aligned too

disagreement: locator: A anchors case_sla_id 2465 with case_id and sla_def_id as cells, B selects case_id = 1233 AND sla_def_id = 6; chose B's because the request fixes no order of SLA rows and the policy's SLA alignment on a move to work may add a response SLA first, which would shift the next id; the selector tests the same row on its natural key, as the benchmark's check does

requirements.text: We just got a flag on the core SQL environment at Acme Systems
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM interaction WHERE interaction_id = 1233 AND case_id = 1233 AND channel = 'alert' AND account_id = 3 AND contact_id = 1 AND status = 'open'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the flag is an inbound contact on the alert channel, and every seed case has one interaction with the case's id, channel, account and contact
channel alert follows the request's 'via Alert Channel'
status open kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
id assumed next in sequence (1233 after 1232); the task creates one interaction

disagreement: cells: A case_id, channel and status, B adds account_id 3 and contact_id 1; chose B's because both added cells are right (the case's account and only contact, as on all 1232 seed interactions) and the predicate is tighter

update_installed_product_details (2).evidence: sys_updated_on is a server-kept timestamp, already non-null for installed product 14 in the seed, so it cannot show the update; the predicate is dropped and status = 'repair' is carried

notes:
The new case's state is not tested: the request does not name one, and 'once the case is ready for work' fixes when the SLA is applied rather than asking for a state change (the policy default for a new case is new).
The case's installed_product_id is not tested: the policy lets a case name a product or an installed product, and forbids attaching an item in repair status to a new case, so whether the case carries installed product 14 depends on the order of the steps.
The case's short_description follows only the policy's format template, which the benchmark does not test, so it is left out.
Acme Systems has an active entitlement for product 48 (entitlement 19, product-specific, unlimited cases), so the case is in scope for SLAs. No response SLA is required: the request names only the resolution SLA.
No benchmark check covers adding Stephanie Todd to CSM Tier 1 Support, so that requirement is new.
The acting user, Karen Watkins, is an admin, and the policy has the assistant act with admin rights by default, so the membership change and the asset status change are within scope.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that Acme Systems' other installed products stay out of repair: one pass wrote it, the other did not; kept because the asset is named by description ('the server running MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 28'), and the account's HPE ProLiant and Dell PowerEdge servers are what a loose reading of 'the server' would sweep in, the boundary of that selector.
disagreement: value: the locator of the new resolution SLA row: one pass the next id 2465, the other case 1233 and sla_def 6; chose the case and definition, since a response SLA aligned first would shift the id.
disagreement: value: the cells of the new interaction: one pass case, channel and status, the other also account 3 and contact 1; chose the tighter set, whose added cells match every seed interaction. The other requirement texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
